key_insight: Se/ZnMgO self-powered photodiodes can both read and update synaptic weight at zero bias, with the sign of plasticity controlled by photon energy: UV light potentiates while visible light depresses.
engineering_relevance: This enables low-power optoelectronic synapses for embedded vision hardware, where sensing, memory, and computation are integrated without an external read voltage.
method: Fabricated Se/ZnMgO thin-film photodiodes and tested zero-bias photocurrent as the synaptic state signal.
Applied wavelength-selective light pulses and measured bidirectional weight updates under varying flux.
Used optical and drift-diffusion simulations to link plasticity to defect filling at the Se/ZnMgO interface.
evidence_signal: At equal photon flux, 365 nm pulses increased photocurrent by 38% while 455 nm pulses decreased it, with up to 19 distinguishable levels per branch; a digit-recognition network reached 89% accuracy without noise and 85% with measured noise.
watch_item: Performance depends on interface defect population and light spectrum, so fabrication variability and spectral control may strongly affect reproducibility and deployment.
paper_title: Wavelength-selective bidirectional plasticity in self-powered Se/ZnMgO visual synapses
